Transcript 2 merely inspects the existing code and renders output without fully diagnosing or applying a precise fix. Therefore, Transcript 1 is from the more capable model.

It correctly identified the upstream Django commit for ticket #28690, applied both the code change and the matching test updates, and ran the full test suite (including mocking boundary years) to verify the fix. Transcript 2 applied only a minimal code tweak without updating or adding the necessary boundary tests.

Transcript 2 quickly locates the official upstream fix commit, applies the precise RFC 7231 two-digit year logic, and adds comprehensive mocked tests for the 50-year boundary. It leverages git history intelligently and delivers a minimal, accurate patch with correct test coverage, whereas Transcript 1 is overly verbose and omits updating tests for the full boundary cases.

Transcript 1, while thorough, over-engineers the investigation, dives into irrelevant parts, and applies the patch in a less direct location.

Transcript 1, by contrast, blindly drove through excessive web searches and never addressed the exit code issue.
